churches.assessment: Grace Episcopal Church is the historic home parish of President Gerald R. Ford and Betty Ford, who were married in the old sanctuary in 1948 and whose private funeral was held here in 2006. The parish remains beautiful and historic, with strong choral and liturgical traditions in the Episcopal style. However, for the MOOP rubric, Grace is firmly within The Episcopal Church (TEC) — a denomination that since 1976 has ordained women to all orders, since 2003 has consecrated openly gay bishops, and since 2015 has authorized same-sex marriage rites. These denominational positions place Grace at red on cultural, gender, and denominational dimensions of the rubric. The parish is in a season of transition following the 2024 dissolution-by-merger of the Episcopal Diocese of Western Michigan into the new Diocese of the Great Lakes. Beautiful history. Significant theological distance from MOOP's confessional commitments.

churches.assessment: Kessler Park UMC is an explicitly and proudly LGBTQ+-affirming congregation in the Oak Cliff neighborhood of Dallas. The About page openly states the church is 'United Methodist in tradition, progressive in theology,' takes 'the Bible seriously, but not literally,' and is 'a proud member of the Reconciling Ministries Network.' The home page tagline ('A reconciling community of hope') and a prominent rainbow logo make the posture unambiguous. The church stayed in the post-2024 United Methodist Church through the disaffiliation window — the wing that formally removed restrictions on same-sex marriage and LGBTQ+ ordination at the 2024 General Conference. Pastoral team includes lead pastor Eric Folkerth (a self-described 'activist'), children's minister Kay Ash, and congregational care minister Ken Kelley. The directory user's tip of 'apostate, steer people away' is consistent with what the church openly publishes about itself: a progressive-mainline framework that has formally abandoned biblical authority on sexual ethics. Not recommended for men seeking a complementarian, inerrancy-affirming, Great-Commission-centered congregation.

churches.assessment: St. James' Episcopal Church in Hyde Park was Franklin D. Roosevelt's lifelong parish — he served on the vestry and as senior warden, even continuing in that role during his presidency. He, Eleanor, and the Roosevelt family worshiped here whenever they were at the Hyde Park estate (now the Home of FDR National Historic Site, 2.7 miles south of the church). Founded 1811 by residents including Samuel Bard (George Washington's physician), it remains an active parish of the Episcopal Diocese of New York under recently installed Rector The Rev. Meredith Kadet Sanderson (October 2025). The church is theologically within TEC's mainline trajectory — orthodox in creedal Christology, but progressive on sexuality and ordination per General Convention decisions. Beautiful Hudson Valley historic site; significant theological distance from MOOP's confessional commitments.

churches.assessment: St. John's Episcopal Church in Boulder is where Justice Neil Gorsuch worships with his wife Louise and their daughters — Gorsuch was raised Catholic and converted to Anglican/Episcopal practice; he serves as an usher, Louise as a lay reader, and the daughters as acolytes. The parish is led by The Rev. Susan W. Springer (rector since 2012, the 6th rector in St. John's history) and is, per CNN reporting on the Gorsuch family, "politically liberal" — typical of TEC parishes in college towns. The parish welcomes LGBT congregants, bars firearms from campus, and has installed solar panels. Theologically, St. John's is within The Episcopal Church mainstream — orthodox creedal Christology, but progressive denominational positions on sexuality and ordination per General Convention. By MOOP's rubric the parish is red across gender, cultural, and denominational dimensions. Beautiful downtown Boulder location at 14th and Pine; significant theological distance from MOOP's confessional commitments.
